_purpose: Authoritative list of vulnerability classes for wpsentinel. Written to disk so the plan survives crashes and any agent can resume without re-deriving it.

classes.title: Stored XSS (contributor+ and unauthenticated)
classes.rationale: Largest single class in the corpus. Contributor+ stored XSS alone is 997 records (~18% of everything).

classes.title: Missing or insufficient capability check
classes.rationale: Second largest. The archetypal WP bug: a handler that never calls current_user_can().

classes.title: Local file inclusion / RFI
classes.rationale: Present.

classes.title: Reflected XSS
classes.rationale: Present.

classes.title: Privilege escalation
classes.rationale: Highest average CVSS in the corpus (9.03).

classes.title: SQL injection via unprepared $wpdb queries
classes.rationale: Highest-impact common class; $wpdb->prepare misuse has very recognizable signatures.

classes.title: Arbitrary file upload to RCE
classes.rationale: Present.

classes.title: PHP object injection via unserialize
classes.rationale: Present.

classes.title: Command injection / eval / dynamic callable
classes.rationale: Rare but avg CVSS 8.86; call_user_func on request data is a recurring WP idiom.

classes.title: Authentication bypass
classes.rationale: avg CVSS 8.89. Social-login and OTP flows dominate recent cases.

classes.title: Missing/incorrect nonce verification
classes.rationale: Distinct from WP-AUTHZ: nonce proves intent, capability proves permission. Needs its own rules.

classes.title: Arbitrary file deletion
classes.rationale: Present.

classes.title: Arbitrary file read / download
classes.rationale: Distinct from WP-LFI: the file is returned, not executed.

classes.title: XML external entity and unsafe XML parsing
classes.rationale: Only 2 in the Wordfence listing but NVD carries more; cheap to detect, severe when present.

classes.title: Sensitive information disclosure
classes.rationale: Often the pivot that makes another bug exploitable (leaked nonces, keys, user email).

classes.title: Unprotected admin-ajax handlers (wp_ajax_nopriv)
classes.rationale: WP-specific ENTRY POINT class. wp_ajax_nopriv_ exposes a handler to the world; the detection signature is registration-site, not sink-site, so it cannot live inside WP-AUTHZ.

classes.title: REST routes with weak permission_callback
classes.rationale: WP-specific ENTRY POINT class. '__return_true' as permission_callback is a one-line signature that WP-AUTHZ's sink-side rules would miss entirely.

classes.title: Arbitrary option/settings update leading to takeover
classes.rationale: WP-specific: writing users_can_register + default_role, or a mail setting, converts a weak update handler into full site takeover. A named class makes the escalation explicit.

classes.title: Hardcoded credentials and weak randomness
classes.rationale: Static-analysis-friendly and common in themes/plugins; rand() used for tokens, keys in source.

classes.title: Server-side request forgery
classes.rationale: wp_remote_get() on user-controlled URL; WP has no safe-URL helper by default.

classes.title: DOM-based XSS in plugin JS
classes.rationale: Underreported in the corpus (6) because scanners rarely see JS; still worth rules.

classes.title: Path traversal in file writes/moves
classes.rationale: Traversal that lands outside the LFI/read/delete outcomes.

classes.title: Open redirect
classes.rationale: wp_redirect() without wp_safe_redirect(); common phishing pivot.

classes.title: Insecure direct object reference
classes.rationale: Handler authorizes the action but never checks ownership of the target id.

classes.title: Formula (CSV) injection in exported data
classes.rationale: Added after the corpus showed CWE-1236 as the largest CWE with no class: 44 records, 35 distinct CVEs. The Wordfence listing buckets only 1 as 'CSV Injection', so its prevalence there is a naming artifact rather than a measure of rarity.

_ranking_caveat: Classes with wordfence_count 0 (WP-AJAX, WP-REST, WP-OPTIONS, WP-SECRETS) are WordPress-specific patterns that the Wordfence listing does not bucket as its own type -- they are counted inside Authorization Bypass and similar. Their prevalence here is therefore an artifact of the source taxonomy, not a measure of rarity: wp_ajax_nopriv_ and permission_callback=>__return_true are among the most common real findings in plugin code. Treat their rank as a floor, and do not drop them on the basis of this number.
_attribution_note: CWE is a COARSE attribution signal only. Several classes legitimately share a CWE (CWE-79 covers stored, reflected and DOM XSS; CWE-862 covers WP-AUTHZ, WP-AJAX and WP-REST), so a corpus count attributed by CWE alone cannot separate them and will over-count each. The detection rules in each class file are the real discriminator; treat CWE counts as an upper bound per class, never as that class's true frequency.

_known_gaps.name: Improper input validation
_known_gaps.note: Too generic to attribute to one class; it co-occurs with a more specific CWE in most records.
